DISTINCTLY Airthrie
DISTINCTLY Airthrie
DISTINCTLY Airthrie
DISTINCTLY Airthrie
Dean Close Airthrie sits in a beautiful property, with a delightful outdoor playground, within the centre of Regency Cheltenham.
As a small school, we can really concentrate on the individuality of every child, the curiosity that nestles inside and the imagination that makes each so special. Our aim is to allow each child to flourish, through their experience of excellent learning opportunities combined with our values of love, contribution and courage which we focus on every day.
Our unique BEAR programme offers a personalised, evolving approach to learning that nurtures each child’s academic, personal and developmental goals whilst supporting a wide range of needs.
Our wonderful teachers and staff embrace all pupils to find out what makes them light-up, whilst instilling a confidence through focusing on praise. Please come and visit us or find out more about Airthrie. Every day is an open day here.
https://www.deanclose.org.uk/school-life/pre-preparatory-school
https://www.deanclose.org.uk/school-life/preparatory-school/meet-the-headmaster
https://www.deanclose.org.uk/school-life/senior-school/teaching-learning/sixth-form

Faith
Our Christian values underpin all that we do as a school. We believe that building a strong foundation based on Love, Courage and Contribution gives the children the chance to grow long-lasting and positive friendships that are created on shared values. We welcome children and families from all faiths and those of no faith at all, and hope that our inclusive approach ensures questions relating to religion and spirituality can be shared openly.
The Dean Close Foundation Chaplain regularly visits to lead assemblies. We also mark occasions such as Remembrance Day and we hold a whole school Carol service to celebrate Christmas. Awe and wonder should be at the heart of learning and by encouraging children to explore our world to the full, we firmly believe that must include questions around faith.

pageCache.pageTitle: Before & After School Care - Dean Close Airthrie School
pageCache.text:
Before & After School Care
To support busy parents we offer Breakfast Club at 7:40am and early morning drop-off from 8:00am free of charge. There is an extra charge for Breakfast Club.
We also and offer late pick-up 'Late Book' and ‘Teatime Club’ until 5:30pm. Children can play board games or carry out homework tasks, read, etc. In the summer months, Late Book pupils often play in the garden before heading inside to complete homework. Late Book runs from 3:45pm - 4:45pm.
Children staying for Teatime are served a light tea and are able to request from a choice of sandwiches, wraps, crumpets, crackers, yogurt, fresh fruit and salad vegetables. There is an extra charge for this service.

Reception
Reception children continue to follow the Early Years Foundation Stage and the curriculum is carefully structured to enable them to learn through both play-based activities and more adult directed tasks.
Learning through play continues to be a vital part of daily life in Reception, enabling children to grow in confidence, whilst nurturing their interests and curiosities.
Children develop key social skills, learn to communicate about their learning, ask how and why questions, investigate and explore. They make full use of the garden as their 'outdoor' classroom.
During a typical week, the pupils enjoy sessions led by specialist teaching staff covering French, Drama, Music and PE. Cooking is also regularly incorporated into their lessons. Topics are flexible and tailored to the interests of the class. Reception enjoys excellent pupil to staff ratios. This enables us to tailor the curriculum to support individual needs and ensure good progress is made towards achieving the Early Learning Goals. If children require additional support this is identified and implemented promptly. We value parents as partners in their children's learning and encourage daily communication.
Classroom activities are enriched by participation in whole school events. These include weekly assemblies, Forest meetings, the annual Carol Service, and in the Summer term; Sports Day and the Summer Concert. Also, we welcome visits from parents who are able to offer specific knowledge or skill sets relating to our topics, for example parental talks about religious festivals such as Chinese New Year, Diwali and Eid or dentists and doctors to give simple health talks. Additionally, we organise visiting speakers which vary from police officers to The Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust.

Years 1 & 2
Year 1 is a very important time for children at Airthrie School. During this year we witness the children taking great strides in terms of both personal and academic development.
As they move from the Foundation Stage the time spent on play-based activities diminishes and learning becomes more subject based. There is still a strong emphasis on learning through practical activities and we pride ourselves on creating a stimulating, safe and engaging learning environment for our pupils
We recognise and encourage children’s social development, helping them to grow in confidence both with their peers and with adults.
We go on visits to a wide variety of venues. In recent years we have been to The Cheltenham Literature Festival, the Cotswold Farm Park, Cotswold Wildlife Park, kite flying on Crickley Hill and strawberry picking at a local Pick your Own site. We also have a number of invited guests who visit us in the classroom to share their experiences and skills.
In Year 2, whilst following the curriculum of Key Stage 1 pupils are taught to become independent thinkers and by the end of the year they are well prepared to move into Prep.
Lessons are extended, most teaching is activity based and creative minds are still very much encouraged to thrive through weekly art, drama, sport and music lessons.

pageCache.pageTitle: Future Steps Preparation Programme - Dean Close Airthrie School
pageCache.text:
Future Steps Preparation Programme
At Airthrie we want to celebrate every individual and guide families in identifying the right senior school that supports each pupils strengths.
We aim to provide a breadth of choice and assist parents in deciding the best future step for their child. As a large portion of our families choose the Grammar School or Scholarship option, we start preparing for this as part of our curriculum in Years 1 and 2.
In addition to our everyday curriculum, Year 5 and 6 pupils can opt in for extra tuition at after school clubs, designed to help prepare them for both 11+ Grammar and Independent school exams. In order to best prepare for this the club aims to develop key exam skills in Reasoning, Maths and English Comprehension. We can assist parents with choosing the relevant 11+ resources for their child, as well as give 1:1 support where necessary.
Pupils are further supported with mock interview practise with the Head and other senior members of the Dean Close Foundation. This is invaluable experience for pupils who are applying for scholarships and school places in which the senior schools invite the pupils to demonstrate their strengths.
We are fortunate to have so many excellent private and state schools in Cheltenham and as part of our programme we prepare and celebrate the success of every child, whatever their onward educational journey.
I loved Airthrie because of the wide range of lessons, and the family atmosphere. Airthrie is really unique, and because it is a small school, it feels like a second home. You always have something to do at Airthrie, as there are so many extra curricular activities on offer. I feel so prepared for secondary school because the teachers encouraged us to do new things and helped us to excel in our lessons. This has made me confident for the next chapter. I was so sad to leave Airthrie this summer, but in a way that is a good thing, as that shows how brilliant a school it was for me. I felt really comfortable at Airthrie, and even though I started in year 3, it seemed like I had been there since Reception. I immediately slotted in because of all the smiles of the happy people around me, and the fun things to do. "

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs - Dean Close Airthrie School
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs
General Provision
Every child at Airthrie benefits from small class sizes and a home away from home environment to help them thrive. Teachers carefully adapt tasks to match individual abilities and provide in-class support.
If your child is facing barriers to learning, we take a highly responsive approach. We offer tailored classroom adaptations, qualified teachers, teaching assistants, and specialist interventions. Currently, we provide support for:
We also offer some in-house specialist assessments and support you whilst you may seek further assessment for your child. During the admissions process you can meet our SENDCo, Mrs Honesty Walker, to discuss how we can meet your child's needs.
Speech and language needs
Sensory needs
Specific learning difficulty friendly teaching
Universal Provision for every child
Every child in every classroom
With small class sizes, and the support of experienced teachers and teaching assistants, we provide a truly inclusive classroom experience. Our teachers get to know each pupil personally, spend time with them individually each day, and continuously adapt their teaching to meet every child's unique learning pace.
We further enhance classroom learning through the expertise of our Teaching Assistants, SENDCo, Speech and Language Therapist and Occupational Therapist.
We are currently working with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) specialists, Moore House School. Through a year-long partnership we are working with their specialist teachers and Speech and Language therapists to develop our teaching and learning skill set. This will directly benefit our children with DLD, dyslexia, dyspraxia and other Speech Language and Communication needs.
At Dean Close Airthrie, every child has an individual plan tailored to their needs. While you may be familiar with My Plans, My Plan+ or Individual Education Plans, our BEAR Plan follows the same recognised "assess, plan, do, review" process. This approach reflects best practice and meets the requirements for referrals and EHCP applications. Find out more here.
Onsite Speech and Language and Occupational Therapy
At Airthrie our small nurturing environment means that teachers work closely with families to identify needs. This is supported through our BEAR plan process.
We can offer observations and further assessments to screen for possible Special Needs. Our SENDCo can spend time with children and parents so that the individuality of needs can be expressed accurately.
We have weekly visits from our own speech and language therapist and occupational therapist. If required, they can both offer you a comprehensive assessment of your child's needs, deliver 1:1 or group therapy sessions and provide practical advice to support learning and development at both home and school. We work closely to implement their specialist advice for children in the classroom.
Speech and Language Therapist:
Occupational Therapist:
We are experienced in working with families and Local Authorities to provide placements for children . We can provide a timely response to consultations and an accurate assessment of how we can meet a child's needs.
If your child has an EHCP and you are seeking a placement please get in touch with our Admissions Team. We can discuss your child's needs and offer visits and taster days to fully assess our suitability.
As a very small school we can tailor our admission process to your child. There are steps that we will work through with you and your family to ensure that we are the right place and that your child make a successful start with us.
Initial Contact: This may be an email and informal chat or a visit to our Open Day. We are very happy to listen to you, find out about your child's needs and provide a clear picture of what Airthrie provides
Sharing information: We ask that parents share all available information. Its very useful to get a full picture of your child's strengths and needs.
Visits and Taster Days: We can accommodate visits in a variety of formats be that visits with a parent, multiple days or even joining us on school trips. Click here to find out more and get in touch.

With small class sizes, we are able to provide personalised attention to each pupil, ensuring that no one is overlooked. This enables us to stretch every child to their fullest potential, supporting them as they embark on their individual journeys. We encourage our pupils to contribute to adventure, show courage, and explore the world around them whilst feeling safe.
We believe that every child deserves a childhood filled with moments of joy, laughter, and innocence. By creating this safe atmosphere, our pupils are happy. Happy pupils will then flourish academically and emotionally.

Beyond Airthrie
We work closely with parents to explore the ‘best fit’ senior school for their child. Airthrie pupils go on to join a wide range of senior schools, including grammar, state or independent schools.
Our ‘Future Steps Preparation Programme’ helps pupils to achieve the best possible outcome for their next step to the senior school of their choice. We prepare pupils over a three year programme for the grammar tests, or for entrance or scholarship assessments to other independent schools.
We are fortunate to have so many excellent private and state schools in Cheltenham and as part of our programme we prepare and celebrate the success of every child, whatever their onward educational journey.
Here is a list of Senior Schools where our pupils have typically been awarded Scholarships and places to over the years.

Airthrie Alumni
Established in 1940 for pupils evacuated from a School in Margate during the war years, the School is rightly proud of its History.
The caring and homely nature of the School does not stop when pupils complete their education at Airthrie, the School is genuinely interested to keep in contact with past pupils.
The School endeavour to remain in contact with former pupils and staff, by inviting them to events that the school holds for the community as well as keeping them up to date with school news. There is a dedicated school archive overseen by an Archivist, this resource is available to all former pupils and staff and acts as a forum for memories to be shared.
If you require any information or would like to get in touch please contact Claire Haines via email by clicking here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Choose Dean Close Airthrie? - Dean Close Airthrie School
pageCache.text:
Why Choose Dean Close Airthrie?
Why Dean Close Airthrie?
Discover a unique educational setting nestled in the heart of Regency Cheltenham, where learning takes on a whole new dimension. Housed in two charming Victorian houses, Dean Close Airthrie provides an enchanting backdrop for your child's early academic journey.
At Airthrie, we believe in the power of personalised education. With small class sizes, our dedicated teachers provide individual attention, ensuring each student receives the support they need to flourish academically and personally. We understand that a child's wellbeing is just as important as their academic success so pastoral care is delivered by class teachers in our nurturing environment where every child feels valued, supported and encouraged to be their authentic self.
Visitors regularly comment on the atmosphere, saying how warm and friendly they find it, with good relations between staff and pupils. We pride ourselves on the warmth of a true family feel at our school, where every child, from Reception to Year 6, knows one another. Building strong connections and lasting friendships is not just a part of our ethos; it's at the heart of everything we do. Join our close-knit community and discover the difference a supportive environment can make in your child's educational journey.
Classrooms of Care
Our teachers are not just facilitators of knowledge but compassionate mentors who understand the importance of a supportive learning environment. At Dean Close Airthrie, pastoral care is seamlessly woven into the fabric of every lesson, creating a safe haven where students can flourish academically and emotionally.
The BEAR Programme
The BEAR (Bespoke Educational Airthrie Roadmap) programme is a personalised approach supporting each child’s unique learning journey alongside our academically ambitious curriculum. It nurtures well-rounded individuals, offering academic challenge within a calm, supportive environment. Beginning with each child’s dreams and aspirations, BEAR creates a living document that evolves with their growth. Goals are tailored, spanning academic, therapeutic and personal development, with strong collaboration between teachers, specialists, and families to ensure every child’s strengths and aspirations are fully supported.
Adventure in Every Corner
Imagine a school where learning extends beyond the classroom. Our adventure playground is a magical place where creativity knows no bounds. From a treehouse hideaway to a thrilling pirate ship, your child's imagination will soar as they embark on daily adventures with their friends.
From the moment they enter Reception, our pupils discover a journey of experiential learning that extends beyond the four walls of a classroom. From autumn scavenger hunts to the thrill of egg launchers in Year 6, every outdoor learning experience is an opportunity for growth. The practical skills acquired in these lessons are not only enriching but also fun and fulfilling, fostering a love for learning that lasts a lifetime.
Dean Close DNA
Across all ages, the curriculum has weaved within it five key skills for the future, known as the 5Cs: critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, compassion, communication. These will enable our pupils to have the flexibility, resilience and confidence to move onto their chosen senior school as confident individuals that will thrive.
These specific skills have been chosen to help our pupils flourish in the widest sense of the word; careers and future employability are vital, but we also want to enable them to live out our core values of courage and love, contributing to their communities, long after they have moved on from Dean Close Airthrie.
The range of experiences, opportunities and the ethos delivered at school through the values and skills, when fitted together, form a DNA profile which makes every pupil’s experience distinctly Dean Close Airthrie.
Creating Confident Futures
Beyond academics, we focus on preparing your child for their next chapter – secondary school. Our track record speaks for itself, with our pupils transitioning to various secondary schools in the area, including grammar, independent and state schools. Armed with both skills and confidence, nurtured in our close-knit school community, they step into the future ready for success.
Everyone is Individual
At our school, we understand that each child is unique and learns in their own way. That's why our teaching approach is tailored to meet the specific needs of every student. Our lessons are diverse, and our teaching style is adjusted to accommodate individual learning preferences.
Our devoted team of teaching assistants work alongside our teachers, providing additional support in the classroom when needed. This allows us to offer one-to-one attention to students who require it, ensuring that no child is left behind.
Mrs Honesty Walker, our SENDCo (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator), possesses a wealth of knowledge in addressing special educational needs. She regularly engages with class teachers to support classroom adaptations and provides one-to-one sessions for students who require personalised support.
Sporting Facilities
We have a sport-for-all philosophy, actively participating in mixed-gender sports during both regular lessons and after-school clubs. We frequently engage in fixtures against local independent and state primary schools, fostering a sense of competition and camaraderie.
We're fortunate to have access to the outstanding sports facilities of Cheltenham Ladies College, boasting two astro turfs, two sports fields, netball and tennis courts, as well as a 25m swimming pool.
Our dedicated sports teachers are passionate about nurturing pupils' athletic abilities. They ensure that all children are encouraged to participate in a variety of sports, ranging from hockey and netball to football and cricket. Additionally, swimming lessons are conducted on a weekly basis throughout the year, emphasising the importance of water safety and proficiency.
One Happy Family
At our school, we're not just a community; we're a family. Each of our families is known and cherished here, creating a warm and inclusive atmosphere that visitors can't help but notice. Our welcoming and friendly environment is a hallmark of our school, leaving a lasting impression on all who walk through our doors. It's no surprise that many of our students' parents were once Airthrie pupils themselves, fondly remembering their early educational experiences and wishing the same for their own children.
All of our pupils know each other by name and eagerly lend a helping hand whenever needed. A heartwarming example of this is our Year 6 pupils dedicating time each week to read with our Year 2 pupils, fostering a culture of support that extends throughout our entire school community.
Follow us on Instagram where we are continually posting news and information about the schools. Use our hashtags to help point you in the direction of what interests you most.

pageCache.pageTitle: About us - The Dean Close Foundation
pageCache.text:
About us
The Dean Close Foundation is a growing, vibrant and diverse family of independent schools and nurseries, uniting around a shared vision and set of values. These spring from the origins of Dean Close School, which was founded in 1886 in memory of Dean Francis Close, Rector of Cheltenham and educational philanthropist. The Christian ethos of that original school continues today where the aim is that every child should be given the opportunities to flourish, underpinned by its core values of courage, contribution and love which are the guiding principles behind its educational vision.
The Foundation is an educational charity providing support to six schools and nine nurseries within its group, creating a strong community that can share best practice, resources and a secure future. This brings many benefits to each school and nursery, and to each child and staff member within them, providing ambitious strategic leadership as well as creating a strong community that can share best practice, ideas, resources and a secure future.
Our community is everything to us, where we aim to grow and deepen relationships between the family of schools and nurseries, offering outstanding care and education from the first months of life into adulthood.
It might seem impossible to have one overarching aim or ambition for the whole Foundation and everyone within it, given this diversity, but we do have such an aim: that of Flourishing. It is our ambition that every individual, every team, each school or nursery and the whole organisation should Flourish.
